diagnosis: The original development folds calibrated and evaluated inside one recording (held-in-calib prefix -> held-in-minival tail of the same file). Every later-day evaluation crosses a recording boundary (block 1 prefix -> block 2). Supervised repairs that won within-recording dev folds collapsed across recordings; the dev protocol, not the later days, was mismatched.

development_protocol.name: cross-recording forward folds
development_protocol.training: held-in-calib recordings of all preceding held-in days
development_protocol.calibration: first 30 s of the fold day's first held-in-calib recording
development_protocol.evaluation: the fold day's second held-in-calib recording (a different recording, as on later days)

evidence_that_the_protocol_matches_later: Under cross-recording dev folds the previous pipeline's dev-optimal rank-6 alpha moves from 1 to 30-100, and alpha 1 drops to 0.1635 -- the same collapse previously observed on later days -- using held-in data only.

feature_front_end.type: causal running z-score of every stacked feature
feature_front_end.initialization: mean/variance of the first 30 s of the calibration recording (all bins, no labels); training recordings are initialized from their own first 30 s
feature_front_end.update: per 20 ms bin: d = x - mu; mu += k d; var = (1 - k)(var + k d^2); k = 0.02 / tau; output (x - mu) / sqrt(max(var, 1e-8))

disclosure: The investigator knew the earlier later-day results when designing this protocol. No later-day labels were computed for any configuration listed here before this file was committed. The later-day evaluation that follows is reused-data evidence, run once for the frozen choice and its matched baselines.
stop_condition: If the frozen choice does not beat the strongest matched baseline on the seven later days, report that failure and do not reselect.
